courses.subject: AIP
courses.title: Academic Internship
courses.description: Individual placements for field learning. Must be integrated with an academic discipline. A written contract involving all parties will include learning objectives, a paper/project outline, and means of supervision and progress evaluation. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, and a completed and approved Learning Agreement for Special Studies.

courses.subject: AIP
courses.title: Academic Internship Program
courses.description: Individual internship placements integrated with an academic discipline. A written contract involving all parties will include learning objectives, a paper/project outline, and means of supervision and progress evaluation. Consent of faculty adviser and program chair required. May be taken for credit up to three times for a maximum of sixteen units.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; department approval.

courses.subject: AIP
courses.title: UCDC: Washington, DC Internship
courses.description: This internship is attached to the University of California, Washington Center programs. Students participating in the campus UCDC program secure internships in the Washington, DC area requiring 18–30 hours per week. Students must be enrolled in the UCDC program.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; department approval.

courses.subject: AIP
courses.title: Public Service Internship
courses.description: Individual placements for field learning performed in nonprofit organizations or government agencies dedicated to providing services in the areas of education, government, social issues, and health. May be taken for credit up to three times for a maximum of twelve units. Contract completed prior to start of internship will include intellectually unified expectations and means of supervision. Faculty member and student will meet regularly.
courses.prerequisites_text: ninety units completed; 2.5 minimum cumulative GPA; department approval.

courses.subject: AAS
courses.title: Introduction to African American Studies
courses.description: This course will cover the experiences of peoples of African descent in the U.S. and broader African Diaspora from the vantage points of cultural production, political practice, socioeconomic conditions, and the overall struggle for social justice along intersecting lines of race, gender, and class. Topics reviewed include slavery (and slave rebellion), Reconstruction, Jim Crow apartheid, the Great Migration and Harlem Renaissance, and the Civil Rights and Black Power Movements.

courses.subject: AAS
courses.title: Legacies of Research on Disenfranchised Communities
courses.description: Students will learn about the historic and current legacies of scientific research and the convergence(s) between science and society as a mechanism for colonization and imperialism.

courses.subject: AAS
courses.title: Directed Group Study in African American Studies
courses.description: Directed group study on a topic or in a field not included in the regular curriculum by special arrangement with a faculty member. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing unless otherwise authorized. Completion of ninety units of undergraduate study, and completion and approval of the Special Studies form.

courses.subject: AAS
courses.title: Independent Study in African American Studies
courses.description: Individual research and study on a particular subject related to African American studies by special arrangement with and under the direction of a faculty member. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Enrollment via the faculty director of the Black Diaspora and African American Studies program only.

courses.subject: AWP
courses.title: Analytical Writing
courses.description: AWP 3 provides writers the opportunity to develop their critical thinking and writing abilities. At the end of AWP 3, students will produce a portfolio of work that will determine their readiness to enter the college writing programs. Replaced AWP 1. Students may take AWP 3, AWP 1, and ELWR 1 for a combined total of three times to earn a grade of C or better to satisfy the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement.

courses.subject: AWP
courses.title: Analytical Writing and Academic English A
courses.description: AWP 4A is the first of a two-quarter sequence designed to offer students who need extra English language support and/or more time to develop their critical thinking and writing abilities. Students who enroll in AWP 4A are required to enroll in AWP 4B in the subsequent quarter. Pass/Not Pass only. Replaced AWP 2A. Students may not receive credit for AWP 4A and AWP 2A or ELWR 2A. Students must earn a grade of Pass to move on to AWP 4B.

courses.subject: AWP
courses.title: Analytical Writing and Academic English B
courses.description: AWP 4B is the second of a two-quarter sequence designed to offer students who need extra English language support and/or more time to develop their critical thinking and writing abilities. At the end of AWP 4B, students will produce a portfolio of work that will determine their readiness to enter the college writing programs. Replaced AWP 2B. Students may not receive credit for AWP 4B and AWP 2B or ELWR 2B. Students must earn a grade of C or better in AWP 4B to satisfy the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement. If a grade of C or better is not earned, students are placed in AWP 3.
courses.prerequisites_text: AWP 4A.

courses.subject: AWP
courses.title: Language and Learning in the American Academy
courses.description: This remote analytical writing course provides students a critical lens through which they can explore debates about identity, language, and learning in higher education. In this course, students engage in critical thinking, reading, and writing practices necessary for success in the American academy. Students may not receive credit for AWP 10 and AWP 10R.

courses.subject: ANBI
courses.title: Human Evolution
courses.description: Major stages of human evolution including the fossil evidence for biological and cultural changes through time.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANBI
courses.title: Human Sexuality in an Evolutionary Perspective
courses.description: This course examines how human sexuality evolved and how it is similar/dissimilar to that of other primates. The topics include the evolution of mating strategies and parenting strategies including the role of sexual selection and how hormones control these behaviors.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANBI
courses.title: Evolution of Human Disease
courses.description: The course will explore the major epidemiological transitions from ape-like ancestors to foraging tribes, farmers, and pastoralists to the global metropolitan primate we now are. We will focus on how diseases have shaped humans and how humans have shaped disease.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANBI
courses.title: Human Anatomy
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the internal structure of the human body through dissection tutorials on CD-ROM.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANBI
courses.title: Social and Behavioral Epigenetics
courses.description: This course is a seminar where we will discuss the latest scientific research in epigenetic mechanisms (changes to gene expression without changing underlying DNA sequences) and their role in regulating health and behavior of humans and other mammals in response to environmental stimuli. Our focus will be on publications related to social and behavioral epigenetics phenomena. Recommended preparation: students should have research experience in a molecular lab.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. ANBI 130 or ANBI 131 or ANBI 134 or ANBI 135 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ANBI
courses.title: Conservation and the Media: Film Lab
courses.description: Conservation on a human-dominated planet is a complex topic. Sometimes a picture is worth a thousand words. This course explores how films about conservation and the human predicament tackle current problems. What makes them effective and what makes them “fail”? We view one film a week and discuss it based on articles and books about that week’s topic.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANAR
courses.title: Special Topics in Anthropological Archaeology
courses.description: Course will vary in title and content. When offered, the current description and title is found in the current Schedule of Classes and the Department of Anthropology website. May be taken for credit four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ANAR
courses.title: Foundations of Archaeology
courses.description: As part of the broad discipline of anthropology, archaeology provides the long chronological record needed for investigating human and social evolution. The theories and methods used in this field are examined. (Archaeology core sequence course.) Recommended preparation: ANTH 3.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANAR
courses.title: Mesopotamia: The Emergence of Civilization
courses.description: This course explores in detail the rise of the world’s earliest cities and states in Mesopotamia and the ancient Near East during the fourth millennium B.C.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANAR
courses.title: Study Abroad: Ancient Mesoamerica
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the archaeology of Mesoamerica and will provide students with the opportunity to gain practical skills from the field. Students will learn hands on by visiting significant ancient cities and museums in Mexico and Central America. Students may receive a combined total of twelve units for ANAR 155 and ANAR 155S. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: students must apply to study abroad program and obtain consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Human Origins
courses.description: An introduction to human evolution from the perspective of physical anthropology, including evolutionary theory and the evolution of the primates, hominids, and modern humans. Emphasis is placed on evidence from fossil remains and behavioral studies of living primates.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Global Archaeology
courses.description: This course examines theories and methods used by archaeologists to investigate the origins and nature of human culture and its materiality. Case studies from the past and present, and digital heritage are explored.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Words and Worlds: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
courses.description: How does language shape the worlds we live in? How do we shape the world through language? This course uses linguistic anthropology to expose and rethink fundamental assumptions about everything from time, space, and materiality to gender, race, and politics in the United States.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Climate Justice
courses.description: This course explores the concept of climate justice in terms of race, ethnicity, cultural heritage, gender, age, religion, language, disabilities, and socioeconomic status. Relates the findings of environmental science to issues of diversity, equity, and inclusion. Explores ethics in terms of the human dimensions of climate change.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Race and Racisms
courses.description: Why does racism still matter? How is racism experienced in the United States and across the globe? With insights from the biology of human variation, archaeology, colonial history, and sociocultural anthropology, we examine how notions of race and ethnicity structure contemporary societies.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Debating Multiculturalism: Race, Ethnicity, and Class in American Societies
courses.description: This course focuses on the debate about multiculturalism in American society. It examines the interaction of race, ethnicity, and class, historically and comparatively, and considers the problem of citizenship in relation to the growing polarization of multiple social identities.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: First-year Student Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Student Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year student seminars are offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges. Topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Sociocultural Anthropology
courses.description: A systematic analysis of social anthropology and of the concepts and constructs required for cross-cultural and comparative study of human societies.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Climate Change, Race, and Inequality
courses.description: This course introduces students to the ways in which climate change exacerbates environmental racism and inequality. We will consider the ways that structural violence and discriminatory policies create environmental inequalities where marginalized communities take on more of the risk and burdens of climate change. We will address community organizing and social justice efforts to combat the systems of power that unevenly distribute the burdens of climate change to marginalized communities.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Climate Change, Cultural Heritage, and Vulnerability
courses.description: Cultural heritage is a human right that is threatened by climate change. This course introduces students to the concept of heritage, how multiple historical and ancient processes influence social vulnerabilities, and what challenges are being faced in the context of changing climate. We will explore the formation and meanings of tangible and intangible heritage, its relation to traditional knowledge and the roles of knowledge over social vulnerability.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: The Climate Change Seminar
courses.description: Explores climate change from the perspectives of biological, archaeological, sociocultural, and medical anthropology and global health. Students develop projects on key topics, such as food, health, sustainability, political economy, and the interaction of ecological and human processes across local, regional, and global scales. Examines social impacts and existential risks. Considers questions related to public policy, education, ethics, and interdisciplinary research collaboration.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Climate Action Scholars: Capstone Project
courses.description: In the second course of this series, students will deepen and apply their knowledge of the diverse ways the climate crisis manifests and interacts with local conditions and histories of inequity and injustice. Students will continue to participate in collaborative learning and community-based research. In addition, they will develop and implement a capstone, “climate action project,” in collaboration with local community partners.
courses.prerequisites_text: ANTH 128A or USP 128A.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Honors Studies in Anthropology
courses.description: A weekly research seminar where students share, read, and discuss in-depth research findings resulting from ANTH 196A and 196B along with selected background literature used in each individual thesis. Students are also taught how to turn their theses into brief presentations for both specialized and broader audiences. Students will be offered opportunities to present their findings at campus events and outreach events during the quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: ANTH 196A-B.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study on a topic or in a field not included in the regular departmental curriculum by special arrangement with a faculty member. Student may take this course twice for credit. Please note: majors may only apply eight units of approved P/NP credit toward the major, and minors may only apply four units of P/NP credit toward the minor. Please contact the department for a list of courses you may take on a P/NP basis and apply toward the major or minor.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and upper-division standing with minimum GPA of 2.5 and completed and approved Special Studies form. Department approval required. (Formerly known as ANPR 198.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study and research under the direction of a member of the faculty. Student may take this course twice for credit. Please note: majors may only apply eight units of approved P/NP credit toward the major, and minors may only apply four units of P/NP credit toward the minor. Please contact the department for a list of courses you may take on a P/NP basis and apply toward the major or minor.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and upper-division standing with minimum GPA of 2.5 and completed and approved Special Studies form. Department approval required. (Formerly known as ANPR 199.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Special Topics in Anthropology Graduate Studies
courses.description: Course will vary in title and content. When offered, the current description and title is found in the current Schedule of Classes and the Department of Anthropology website. (Can be taken a total of four times as topics vary.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Department Colloquium
courses.description: A forum to present work by faculty, students, and guests. Course will be offered quarterly.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (S/U grades only.) (Formerly known as ANGR 230.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Seminar in Science Studies
courses.description: (Cross-listed with COGR 225B, HIGR 239, PHIL 209B, and SOCG 255B.) Study and discussion of a selected topic in the science studies field with an emphasis on the development of research and writing skills. The topic varies from year to year. ANTH 272, COGR 225B, HIGR 239, PHIL 209B, and SOCG 255B may be repeated and taken for credit in any combination for a combined total of six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Colloquium in Science Studies
courses.description: (Cross-listed with COGR 225C, HIGR 240, PHIL 209C, and SOCG 255C.) A forum for the presentation and discussion of research in progress in science studies by graduate students, faculty, and visitors. Students must attend the colloquium series for their entire first and second years. ANTH 273, COGR 225C, HIGR 240, PHIL 209C, and SOCG 255C may be repeated and taken for credit in any combination for a combined total of two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Archaeology Practicum
courses.description: Field and laboratory training for graduate students in archaeology. Students will design and implement archaeological fieldwork or analyze data collected in the field.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of the instructor. (Formerly known as ANGR 288.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Master’s Thesis Preparation
courses.description: The student will work on the master’s thesis under the direction of the departmental committee chair. The course will be taken in the student’s second year. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate student in anthropology and consent of master’s thesis chair. (Formerly known as ANGR 295.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Dissertation Fieldwork Proposal Preparation
courses.description: The student will work in cooperation with his or her departmental committee to develop a research proposal for the doctoral research project. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in anthropology and consent of departmental committee chair. (Formerly known as ANGR 296A/296B.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Supervised study of individually selected anthropological topics under the direction of a member of the faculty. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (Formerly known as ANGR 298.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: PhD candidacy in anthropology. (Formerly known as ANGR 299.)

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Anthropology graduate students participate in the undergraduate teaching program during one quarter anytime in the first four years of residence. Teaching may be in the anthropology department or other departments or programs on campus. Equivalent to duties expected of a fifty percent TA. Enrollment in four units documents the PhD requirement. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate student in anthropology. (Formerly known as ANGR 500.)

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Special Topics in Sociocultural Anthropology
courses.description: Course usually taught by visiting faculty in sociocultural anthropology. Course will vary in title and content. When offered, the current description and title is found in the current Schedule of Classes and the Department of Anthropology website. May be taken for credit four times as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Aging: Culture and Health in Late Life Human Development
courses.description: (Cross-listed with GLBH 101.) Examines aging as process of human development, from local and global perspectives. Focuses on the interrelationships of social, cultural, psychological, and health factors that shape the experience and well-being of aging populations. Students explore the challenges and wisdom of aging. Students may not receive credit for GLBH 101 and ANSC 101.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Transgenderisms
courses.description: This course contrasts mainstream Anglo-American conceptualizations of transgenderism with ethnographic accounts of the experiences and practices of gender expansive people of color (African, Native, Asian/Pacific Islander, and Latinx Americans) in the U.S. and abroad. It will question the idea of transgenderism as a crossing from one gender to another one, the distinction between gender identity and sexuality, and the analytic of intersectionality. Students will not receive credit for both CGS 117 and ANSC 117.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: The Politics of Environmental Change
courses.description: In this course, we will explore how people advocating for environmental change works. We will study the theory of social change, including the discourses of nature and culture that underlie contemporary societies. We will study the ways political decisions are made and how policy makers are influenced. Given the enormity of what is at stake—climate change and increasing environmental precarity—how can we harness politics to transform our world?
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Chinese Popular Religion
courses.description: The religious world of ordinary precommunist times, with some reference to major Chinese religious traditions. Recommended preparation: background in premodern Chinese history.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Global Health and the Environment
courses.description: (Cross-listed with GLBH 147.) Examines interactions of culture, health, and environment. Rural and urban human ecologies, their energy foundations, sociocultural systems, and characteristic health and environmental problems are explored. The role of culture and human values in designing solutions will be investigated. Students may not receive credit for both GLBH 147 and ANSC 147.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Global Health and Cultural Diversity
courses.description: (Cross-listed with GLBH 148.) Introduction to global health from the perspective of medical anthropology on disease and illness, cultural conceptions of health, doctor-patient interaction, illness experience, medical science and technology, mental health, infectious disease, and health-care inequalities by ethnicity, gender, and socioeconomic status. May be coscheduled with ANTH 248. Students may not receive credit for both GLBH 148 and ANSC 148.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Ethnography in Practice
courses.description: This practicum course provides firsthand experience with ethnography, a form of qualitative social research based on interviews, observations, and other methods. Each student will design, carry out, and report on a small-scale ethnographic research project of personal interest. This course emphasizes experiential learning, discussion, and writing, with some on-campus group observations and supplementary readings and videos.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Capitalism and Gender
courses.description: (Cross-listed with CGS 120.) Drawing insight from anti-colonial and queer of color critique, this course critically examines the demands capitalism makes on us to perform gender, and how that relates to processes of exploitation and racialization. We will explore alternatives and develop strategies for navigating jobs in this system. Students may receive credit for one of the following: CGS 120, CGS 180, and ANSC 180. CGS 120 is renumbered from CGS 180.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ANSC
courses.title: Stories and Selves
courses.description: If you conduct ethnographic research, you will inevitably find yourself dealing with stories. They play a huge role in human interaction, and they shape us in fundamental ways. This class includes a workshop component in which students collect narratives through ethnographic methods and learn how to analyze them anthropologically.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Galaxies and the Universe
courses.description: An introduction to galaxies and cosmology. Topics include gravity and motion, atomic structure and light, the Milky Way, galaxy types and distances, dark matter, large scale structure, the expansion of the universe, dark energy, and the early universe.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Astronomy in Science Fiction
courses.description: Survey of current topics in astrophysics from the perspective of astronomy in science fiction. The course will consist of readings in selected science fiction novels, watching relevant films, companion readings in an introductory astronomy text, and critical analysis and discussion.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Additional Topics in Classical Physics
courses.description: This course explores topics in classical physics with the intent of preparing students from the Physics 2 sequence for upper-division astronomy and astrophysics major courses. Topics include energy methods, rotational motion, coupled oscillators, waves in continua, basic fluids, hydrostatics, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves and radiation, optics, thermodynamics, and acoustics.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or PHYS 2AR and PHYS 2B and PHYS 2C and PHYS 2D.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Antiracism in Physics and Astronomy
courses.description: How racism manifests and is sustained by the ideas, practices, and structures of modern physics and astronomy, and how to create antiracist interventions. Topics include the history of scientific racism, how racism and science remain entwined through language, community, visibility, and practices, how racial barriers to participation are sustained, and examining effective practices to address barriers and build inclusive communities in the physical sciences.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: First-Year Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year seminars can be offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Students may complete up to four first-year seminars with the stipulation that none of the seminars are repeated.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Dynamics of Radiation and Fluids
courses.description: Electromagnetic radiation and topics in fluid dynamics with an emphasis on astrophysical applications. Topics include special relativity, radiation: multipole expansion, Lienard-Wiechert formulation, radiation from relativistic charges; electromagnetic scattering, topics in radiation processes, introductory fluids, Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, potential flow and induced mass, vorticity, convection and Schwarzchild criterion, and turbulence.
courses.prerequisites_text: ASTR 102.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics of Radiation, Atoms and Molecules
courses.description: This course discusses quantum mechanical applications of astrophysical interest, with an emphasis on radiation processes. Topics include electromagnetic field and time-dependent perturbation theory, transitions, and Fermi’s golden rule; absorption cross sections, selection rules, single and multi-electron atoms, and diatomic molecules, including the Born-Oppenheimer approximation; physics of the chemical bond and an introduction to the Dirac equation.
courses.prerequisites_text: ASTR 105.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Galaxies
courses.description: An in-depth exploration of the structure and properties of galaxies in the universe. Topics covered include the Milky Way, the interstellar medium, properties of spiral and elliptical galaxies, rotation curves, starburst galaxies, galaxy formation and evolution, large-scale structure, and active galaxies and quasars.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A/2AR-B-C-D or 4A-B-C-D-E.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Data Science in Astronomy
courses.description: Introduction to statistical and machine learning methods and algorithms frequently used in modern astronomy research. The Python programming language will be used almost exclusively due to its widespread usage in astronomy. The course will use a variety of cutting-edge data science tools, techniques, and numerical methods widely used in the astronomy community, with an emphasis on utilizing publicly available codes. May be coscheduled with ASTR 254.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A/2AR-B-C-D or 4A-B-C-D-E and BILD 62 or COGS 18 or CSE 11 or CSE 6R or CSE 8A or CSE 8B or DSC 10 or PHYS 41.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. Department approval required. Upper division standing required. May be taken for credit up to three times.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Stellar Structure and Evolution
courses.description: Energy generation, flow, hydrostatic equilibrium, equation of state. Dependence of stellar parameters (central surface temperature, radius, luminosity, etc.) on stellar mass and relation to physical constants. Relationship of these parameters to the HR diagram and stellar evolution. Stellar interiors, opacity sources, radiative and convective energy flow. Nuclear reactions, neutrino processes. Polytropic models. White dwarfs and neutron stars. Renumbered from PHYA 223. Students may not receive credit for both ASTR 211 and PHYA 223.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Astronomy and Astrophysics Colloquium
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in astronomy and astrophysics relevant to the entire field. May be taken for credit up to twenty-one times.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Astronomy and Astrophysics Journal Club
courses.description: Student and researcher led discussion on current research in astronomy and astrophysics. May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Directed Studies in Astronomy and Astrophysics
courses.description: Research studies under the direction of a faculty member. May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times. Department approval required.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Thesis Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
courses.description: Directed research on dissertation topic once a PhD candidate is approved. May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times. Department approval required.

courses.subject: AUD
courses.title: Preceptorship in Neuro-Otology
courses.description: Observations in UC San Diego Otology clinic. Learn about procedures for taking histories and performing clinical examinations, patient treatment, and patient education from otologists.
courses.prerequisites_text: second-year AuD student or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AUD
courses.title: Advanced Diagnostics in Audiology
courses.description: This course describes advanced assessment including tinnitus assessment, tuning fork tests, Eustachian tube dysfunction tests, sound sensitivity assessment, and automated audiograms. Assessment methods, clinical research, and pathology will be discussed. Students will gain hands-on experience through laboratory assignments.
courses.prerequisites_text: second-year AuD student or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AUD
courses.title: Central Auditory Processing Assessment and Management
courses.description: Central auditory processing assessment and management for pediatrics and adults. Focus on behavioral tests assessing dichotic listening, temporal processes, pattern recognition, performance with competing and degraded signals.
courses.prerequisites_text: course restricted to AuD students.

courses.subject: AUD
courses.title: Intraoperative Monitoring
courses.description: Methods and procedures required for monitoring of evoked auditory responses in the operating room. The indications for the use of intraoperative monitoring and difficulties unique to this setting. The course will include the opportunity to observe auditory potential monitoring in the operating room.
courses.prerequisites_text: second- or third-year AuD student or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AUD
courses.title: Clinical Practice in Audiology II
courses.description: Applications of clinical procedures to patient assessment. Includes clinical observation, interaction with otologists, and supervised patient care involving diagnostics and hearing-aid evaluations in the UC San Diego audiology clinics. This course may be taken more than once.
courses.prerequisites_text: open to second- or third-year doctoral students or consent of instructor. One quarter unit represents three to four hours per week. Must also be concurrently enrolled in AUD 291.

courses.subject: AUD
courses.title: Clinical Case Studies/Staffing
courses.description: Presentations and discussion of clinical cases and issues related to clinical practice. Students’ clinical experiences are discussed relative to medical and audiological assessment and management. This course may be taken more than once.
courses.prerequisites_text: second- or third-year AuD student or consent of instructor. Must be taken more than once.

courses.subject: AUD
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Participation in specific faculty research activities. Become familiar with research methods and objectives of a faculty’s research project. Participate in data collection and analysis at the discretion of the faculty investigator.
courses.prerequisites_text: second- or third-year AuD student and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AUD
courses.title: Doctoral Project
courses.description: Individual investigation and preparation of the doctoral project for the AuD degree will be performed under the supervision of an experienced research mentor.
courses.prerequisites_text: advancement to candidacy in the AuD program.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: First-year Student Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Student Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year student seminars are offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research by arrangement with a bioengineering faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of thirty units of undergraduate study at UC San Diego with a UC San Diego GPA of at least 3.0 and consent of a bioengineering faculty member; completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or research under direction of a member of the faculty.
courses.prerequisites_text: student must be of first-year standing and a Regents Scholar; approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Bioengineers
courses.description: The class provides foundation in probability and statistics. Topics include probability spaces, random variables, independence, common distributions, CLT, estimator accuracy, maximum likelihood, and hypothesis testing. Written problems are provided for each topic. Applications are discussed in regard to bioengineering problems.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 31AH , MATH 20C or MATH 31BH; bioengineering majors only or consent of department. (F,S,Su)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Molecular Components of Living Systems
courses.description: Introduction to molecular structures. Macromolecules and assemblies-proteins, nucleic acids, and metabolites. Principles of design of simple and complex components of organelles, cells, and tissues.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 120 or consent of department. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Mass Transfer
courses.description: Mass transfer in solids, liquids, and gases with application to biological systems. Free and facilitated diffusion. Convective mass transfer. Diffusion-reaction phenomena. Active transport. Biological mass transfer coefficients. Steady and unsteady state. Flux-force relationships. (Credit not allowed for both CENG 101C and BENG 103B.)
courses.prerequisites_text: CENG 101A or MAE 101A or BENG 112A, or consent of department. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Fluid and Cell Biomechanics
courses.description: Fluid hydrostatics and flow dynamics. Flow kinematics and conservation laws applied to the circulation. Viscous biofluids. Biopolymers, cell mechanics, and mechanobiology. Problem solving and design in biofluid and cell mechanics.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 112A or consent of department. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Modeling and Computation in Bioengineering
courses.description: Computational modeling of molecular bioengineering phenomena: excitable cells, regulatory networks, and transport. Application of ordinary, stochastic, and partial differential equations. Introduction to data analysis techniques: power spectra, wavelets, and nonlinear time series analysis.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 122A or BENG 123 or BENG 181 or consent of department. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Biotechnology Thermodynamics and Kinetics
courses.description: An introduction to physical principles that govern biological matter and processes, with engineering examples. Thermodynamic principles, structural basis of life, molecular reactions and kinetics, and models to illustrate biological phenomena.
courses.prerequisites_text: CHEM 6B, MATH 20A, 20B, 20D, PHYS 2A, 2B, 2C; majors only or consent of department. (W)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Measurements, Statistics, and Probability
courses.description: A combined lecture and laboratory course that provides an introductory treatment of probability theory, including distribution functions, moments, and random variables. Practical applications include estimation of means and variances, hypothesis testing, sampling theory, and linear regression.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20D and MATH 18 or MATH 31AH; BENG 100 or consent of department. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Physiology
courses.description: Introductory mammalian physiology for bioengineering students, with emphasis on control mechanisms and engineering principles. Digestive, respiratory, renal, and reproductive systems; regulation of metabolism, and defense mechanisms. (Credit not allowed for both BIPN 102 and BENG 140B.)
courses.prerequisites_text: CHEM 6A or CHEM 6AH and PHYS 2A or PHYS 2AR and PHYS 2B and BILD 1, or BENG 102; majors only or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Chemical and Molecular Bioengineering Techniques
courses.description: Introductory laboratory course in current principles and techniques of chemistry and molecular biology applicable to bioengineering. Quantitation of proteins and nucleic acids by spectrophotometric, immunological, and enzymatic methods. Separations and purification by centrifugation, chromatographic, and electrophoretic methods. Course materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: BICD 100, BENG 100, CHEM 40B or CHEM 40BH or BENG 120, MAE 170; majors only or consent of department. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Biomolecular Engineering
courses.description: Basic molecular biology and recombinant DNA technologies. Structure and function of biomolecules that decode genomes and perform energy conversion, enzymatic catalysis, and active transport. Metabolism of macromolecules. Molecular diagnostics. Design, engineering, and manufacture of proteins, genomes, cells, and biomolecular therapies.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 1 or consent of department. (W)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Laboratory
courses.description: A laboratory course demonstrating basic concepts of biomechanics, bioengineering design, and experimental procedures involving animal tissue. Sources of error and experimental limitations. Computer data acquisition, modeling, statistical analysis. Experiments on artery, muscle and heart mechanics, action potentials, viscoelasticity, electrocardiography, hemorheology. Course materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: MAE 170; junior or senior standing in the major or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Biological Databases
courses.description: (Cross-listed as BIMM 182, CSE 182, and CHEM 182.) This course provides an introduction to the features of biological data, how those data are organized efficiently in databases, and how existing data resources can be utilized to solve a variety of biological problems. Object-oriented databases, data modeling, and data description. Survey of current biological database with respect to above; implementation of database focused on a biological topic.
courses.prerequisites_text: CSE 100; bioinformatics majors only. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Principles of Biomaterials Design
courses.description: Fundamentals of materials science as applied to bioengineering design. Natural and synthetic polymeric materials. Materials characterization and design. Wound repair, blood clotting, foreign body response, transplantation biology, biocompatibility of materials, tissue engineering. Artificial organs and medical devices. Government regulations. Patenting. Economic impact. Ethical issues. A term project and oral presentation are required.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 1 and BENG 130 and PHYS 2A or PHYS 2AR, or consent of department. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Principles of Bioinstrumentation Design
courses.description: Biophysical phenomena, transducers, and electronics as related to the design of biomedical instrumentation. Potentiometric and amperometric signals and amplifiers. Biopotentials, membrane potentials, chemical sensors. Electrical safety. Mechanical transducers for displacement, force, and pressure. Temperature sensors. Flow sensors. Light-based instrumentation.
courses.prerequisites_text: ECE 35 or MAE 40; or consent of department. (W)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Design Project: Planning
courses.description: General engineering design topics including project planning and design objectives, background research, engineering needs assessment, technical design specifications, engineering standards, and design requirements and constraints. Introduction to biomedical and biotechnology design projects. Career and professional advising. Majors must enroll in the course for a letter grade in order to count the sequence toward the major. No exceptions will be approved.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 112A or BENG 152 or BENG 168 or BENG 181; bioengineering, bioengineering: biotechnology, or bioengineering: biosystems majors, or bioengineering: bioinformatics majors only or consent of department. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Design Project: Presentation
courses.description: Oral presentations of design projects, including design, development, and implementation strategies and results of prototype testing. Majors must enroll in the course for a letter grade in order to count the sequence toward the major. No exceptions will be approved.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 187C; bioengineering, bioengineering: biotechnology, or bioengineering: biosystems or bioengineering: bioinformatics majors only or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Special Topics in Bioengineering
courses.description: Course given at the discretion of the faculty on current topics of interest in bioengineering.
courses.prerequisites_text: bioengineering majors only (BE25, BE27, BE28, BE29) or consent of department. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Clinical Experience in Bioengineering
courses.description: Introduction on the integration of bioengineering and clinical medicine through lectures and rotations with clinical faculty. Students will work with clinical mentors and course faculty to identify areas where engineering can improve diagnostics, clinical practice, and/or treatment. May be coscheduled with BENG 294C.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 140A or BIPN 100; BENG 140B or BIPN 102; consent of instructor required. A GPA of 3.5 is requested as a requirement per the agreement with the School of Medicine to ensure that students who are participating in the program have a strong academic background to be in the clinic as an undergraduate. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Industrial Internship
courses.description: Under the joint supervision of a faculty adviser and industry mentor, the student will work at or be mentored at a bioengineering industrial company to gain practical bioengineering experience, summarized in a technical report. May be taken for credit up to three times. With department approval, four units of credit may substitute for a technical elective. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of department and completion of all lower-division course requirements, including general-science requirement; laboratory experience. (F,W,S,Su)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Engineering Internship
courses.description: An enrichment program, available to a limited number of undergraduate students, which provides work experience with industry, government offices, hospitals, and their practices. Subject to the availability of positions, students will work in a local industry or hospital (on a salaried or unsalaried basis) under the supervision of a faculty member and industrial, government, or hospital employee. Prior department approval and final report are required. Units may not be applied toward major graduation requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: completion of ninety units with a 2.5 GPA and approval from a bioengineering faculty coordinator. (F,W,S,Su)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study, on a topic or in a field not included in the regular department curriculum, by arrangement with a bioengineering faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research by arrangement with a bioengineering faculty member. May be taken for credit three times. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form. (F,W,S,Su)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Genomics, Proteomics, and Network Biology
courses.description: Annotating genomes, characterizing functional genes, profiling, reconstructing pathways.
courses.prerequisites_text: Pharm 201, BENG 202/CSE 282, or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Topics in Bioengineering
courses.description: Course given at the discretion of the faculty on current topics of interest in bioengineering. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Continuum Mechanics Applied to Medicine/Biology
courses.description: Introduction to the basic definitions of continuum mechanics and their mathematical formulation at the graduate level with applications to problems in medicine and biology.
courses.prerequisites_text: (BENG 226 or MAE 201 or MAE 210A) and (BENG 227 or MAE 201 or MAE 210A) and (BENG 221 or MAE 208). (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Systems Biology and Bioengineering III: Building and Simulating Large-Scale in Silico Models
courses.description: Analysis of biological data can be performed at four levels: 1) statistical analysis, 2) integration of knowledge, 3) integration of networks, and 4) integration of biophysical laws. This course teaches the last two levels. The third level consists of integrating data in the context of genome-scale models to simulate and predict cellular phenotypes. The fourth level consists of analyzing data in the context of kinetic and thermodynamic laws that govern cellular function.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 212 and graduate standing. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Regulatory Affairs
courses.description: Introduces real-world tools and skills that product development engineers are expected to master in a medical device company. Students will be introduced to all stages of medical device development in an FDA-regulated environment with an emphasis in design controls and building a design history file. Students will also be exposed to other relevant topics such as project management, legal consideration, medical reimbursement, regulatory submissions, commercialization, and product improvements.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in bioengineering only or consent of department.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Foundations of Bioengineering I: Tissue and Cell Properties
courses.description: Modern development of biomechanics at an advanced mathematical level. Description of internal stresses and deformation in living tissues and fluids, thermodynamics. Mechanics of soft connective tissue, extracellular matrix, cells, membranes, and cytoskeleton. Mechanotransduction, migration, adhesion. Blood flow in microvessels. Biomechanical analysis of tissue injury. Recommended preparation: a previous background in biomechanics is strongly recommended prior to taking this course.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Transport Phenomena in Living Systems
courses.description: This course describes the movement of heat and chemical mass in biological systems. Diffusion, convection and biochemical reactions in a variety of biological and engineering examples are analyzed and modeled. Students that have taken BENG 222 cannot take BENG 227 for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 221, graduate standing, or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Cardiovascular Physiology
courses.description: Physical concepts of behavior of heart, large blood vessels, vascular beds in major organs and the microcirculation. Physical and physiological principles of blood flow, blood pressure, cardiac work, electrophysiology of the heart. Special vascular beds, including their biological and hemodynamic importance. Integration through nervous and humoral controls.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 230B or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Musculoskeletal Health, Injury, and Disease
courses.description: An overview of the musculoskeletal system from a bioengineering perspective. Health, injury, disease of bone, cartilage, tendon, ligament, meniscus, synovium, intervertebral disc, skeletal muscle, peripheral nerve. Mechanisms and models underlying current and future therapies.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Neuromuscular Physiology and Biomechanics
courses.description: Mechanical properties of structures involved in movement (muscles, tendons, bones). Models of neuromuscular adaptation to chronic electrical stimulation, voluntary exercise, surgical overload, spinal cord injury, denervation, limb immobilization, exercise-induced injury and muscle regeneration. Stem cells in muscle function and plasticity.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Intro to Neurophysiology: Molecules to Systems
courses.description: Introduction to molecular and cellular neurobiology and their integration with systems neurophysiology. Homeostasis will be an organizing theme. The material will be presented both qualitatively and quantitatively, emphasizing the mathematical, physical, and chemical foundations and dynamics that underlie neurophysiological functions.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Molecular Imaging and Quantitation in Living Cells
courses.description: This course will introduce quantitative fluorescence microscopy techniques for imaging, manipulating, and quantifying the spatiotemporal characteristics of molecular events in live cells. A laboratory component will be integrated with students organized into small teams for projects. Recommended preparation: basic optics at the level of ECE 181, introductory molecular and cellular biology at the level of BIMM 100 and BICD 110, respectively.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Numerical Analysis in Multiscale Biology
courses.description: Introduces mathematical tools to simulate biological processes at multiple scales. Numerical methods for ordinary and partial differential equations (deterministic and stochastic), and methods for parallel computing and visualization. Hands-on use of computers emphasized; students will apply numerical methods in individual projects.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. (W)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Imaging Cardiovascular Disease
courses.description: This course will focus on the imaging modalities used to diagnose and guide treatment of cardiovascular disease such as echocardiography, single photon computed tomography (SPECT), X-ray angiography, computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Seminar in Bioengineering
courses.description: Weekly seminars by faculty, visitors, postdoctoral research fellows, and graduate students concerning research topics in bioengineering and related subjects. May be repeated for credit. Course does not apply toward MS graduation requirements. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Supramolecular Structure Determination Laboratory
courses.description: A laboratory course combining hands-on mass spectrometry and bioinformatics tools to explore the relationship between structure and function in macromolecules. Tools for peptide sequencing, analysis of post-translational modification, and fragmentation analysis by mass spectrometry are examples of experiments students will run.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Statistical Learning in Bioinformatics
courses.description: A hallmark of bioinformatics is the computational analysis of complex data. The combination of statistics and algorithms produces statistical learning methods that automate the analysis of complex data. Such machine learning methods are widely used in systems biology and bioinformatics. This course provides an introduction to statistical learning and assumes familiarity with key statistical methods. Students may not receive credit for BENG 285 and ECE 204 and BNFO 285.
courses.prerequisites_text: ECE 271A or ECE 271B or MATH 283; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Scientific Ethics
courses.description: Lectures, readings, and discussions about the responsible conduct and reporting of research, working with others in science, and social responsibilities; the course is designed as an option for meeting federal regulations for such training. Students should review the following web page prior to enrollment: https://ethics.ucsd.edu/courses/ethics/index.html . (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: doctoral students only or consent of department. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Clinical Experience in Bioengineering
courses.description: Capstone experiential learning course where students are to integrate bioengineering training and clinical medicine through lectures and rotations with clinical faculty. Students will identify problems with diagnostics, clinical practice, and/or treatment, and use engineering principles to design solutions. May be coscheduled with BENG 193.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 294B; bioengineering MS medicine majors only or consent of department.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Design Project and Industrial Training
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students focused on design, applied research, and professional experience.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department approval. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Laboratory Research Rotation
courses.description: Laboratory research rotation for first-year BENG PhD students. Students will write a final paper. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: PhD student in bioengineering. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students engaged in research and writing theses. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Teaching Experience
courses.description: Teaching experience in an appropriate bioengineering undergraduate course under direction of the faculty member in charge of the course. Lecturing one to two hours per week in either a problem-solving section or regular lecture. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department approval. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BNFO
courses.title: Seminar in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology
courses.description: Weekly seminars by faculty and visiting bioinformaticists presenting their research. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit nine times.

courses.subject: BNFO
courses.title: Bioinformatics Student Research Talks
courses.description: Weekly presentations by bioinformatics and systems biology students about research projects that are proposed or completed. Faculty mentors are present to contribute critiques and suggestions. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: bioinformatics and systems biology program graduate students only.

courses.subject: BNFO
courses.title: Statistical Learning in Bioinformatics
courses.description: (Cross-listed with ECE 204 and BENG 285.) A hallmark of bioinformatics is the computational analysis of complex data. The combination of statistics and algorithms produce statistical learning methods that automate the analysis of complex data. Such machine learning methods are widely used in systems biology and bioinformatics. This course provides an introduction to statistical learning and assumes familiarity with key statistical methods. Letter grades only. Students may not receive credit for BNFO 285 and ECE 204 and BENG 285.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 283 or ECE 271A or ECE 271B.

courses.subject: BNFO
courses.title: Scientific Ethics
courses.description: Lectures, readings, and discussions about the responsible conduct and reporting of research, working with others in science, and social responsibilities; the course is designed as an option for meeting federal regulations for such training. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: bioinformatics and systems biology graduate students only. Students should review the following web page prior to enrollment: https://ethics.ucsd.edu/courses/ethics/index.html .

courses.subject: BNFO
courses.title: Research Rotation
courses.description: Laboratory research of special topics under the direction of a program faculty member. The purpose is to train students in specific research methodologies and identify a laboratory in which to pursue doctoral dissertation research. Three quarters are required for PhD candidates. May be taken for credit up to six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: bioinformatics graduate students and consent of instructor and program.

courses.subject: BNFO
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students engaged in research and writing theses. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.
courses.prerequisites_text: bioinformatics and systems biology graduate students and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: BNFO
courses.title: Teaching Assistantship
courses.description: Teaching experience in an appropriate bioinformatics undergraduate or graduate course under direction of the faculty member in charge of the course. Each PhD candidate must complete two academic quarters of experience for S/U grade only. May be taken for credit four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing and consent of instructor (department stamp). (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BIEB
courses.title: Ecology Laboratory
courses.description: A laboratory course to familiarize students with ecological problem solving and methods. Students will perform outdoor fieldwork and use a computer for data exploration and analysis. Fieldwork can be expected in this course. Associated travel may be required, and students are responsible for their own transportation. Students may need to provide and use their own laptop. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: BIEB 100 or MATH 11 or SIO 187 and BILD 3 and BILD 4.

courses.subject: BIEB
courses.title: Genome Diversity and Dynamics
courses.description: Modern sequencing technology has revolutionized our ability to detect how genomes vary in space among individuals, populations, and communities, and over time. This course will review methods and concepts in ecological and evolutionary genomics that help us understand these differences, including their relevance to health (human microbiome, cancer evolution), evolutionary history (ancestor reconstruction, human evolution), and the environment (effect of climate change). Prerequisites : BILD 1 and BILD 3.

courses.subject: BIEB
courses.title: Disease Ecology
courses.description: Infectious diseases have devastating consequences, but vary in attributes. Using an ecological approach, the course will explore why some diseases explode in numbers, when and why new diseases emerge, how infectious disease affects plants and animals, and how can this inform conservation efforts. Students will develop a conceptual framework and quantitative tool set for answering such questions, as well as strategies for managing the emergence and spread of disease on a changing planet. Students will use their own laptops. Prerequisites : BILD 3.

courses.subject: BIEB
courses.title: Evolution of Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Treating infectious diseases is a uniquely difficult problem since pathogens often evolve, rendering today’s therapies useless tomorrow. This course will provide a review of concepts and methods in evolutionary medicine, with an emphasis on microbial genomics and molecular evolution. Prerequisites : BILD 3.

courses.subject: BIEB
courses.title: Evolutionary Inquiry
courses.description: Students will investigate selected in-depth topics in evolutionary biology through reading and writing. Students will read books and articles written for a general audience as well as primary literature. Example topics include the origins of novel features, the impact of human activity and environmental changes on evolutionary processes, the rate and intensity of natural selection, and how our own evolutionary history affects human health. Prerequisites : BILD 1 and BILD 3.

courses.subject: BIEB
courses.title: Microbiome Function Laboratory
courses.description: This course examines current evidence of how host-associated microbiomes contribute toward host phenotypes. The course reviews approaches for studying host-microbiome interactions, including empirical experiments and omics, and the implications of microbiomes in ecology and evolutionary biology. Students will use their own laptop computers. May be coscheduled with BGGN 261. Prerequisites : BILD 1 and BILD 3.

courses.subject: BIEB
courses.title: Behavioral Ecology and Conservation
courses.description: Principles of behavioral ecology from individuals to societies from evolutionary and applied perspectives. Considers how behavior evolves in its environmental context, including human impacts and human-wildlife interactions. Encourages critical engagement with the scientific process and practice, examining inclusion and representation.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 3.

courses.subject: BICD
courses.title: Genetics
courses.description: An introduction to the principles of heredity emphasizing diploid organisms. Topics include Mendelian inheritance and deviations from classical Mendelian ratios, pedigree analysis, gene interactions, gene mutation, linkage and gene mapping, reverse genetics, population genetics, and quantitative genetics. Students may receive credit for one of the following: BICD 100 or BICD 100R.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 1 and BILD 3.

courses.subject: BICD
courses.title: Cell Biology
courses.description: The structure and function of cells and cell organelles, cell growth and division, motility, cell differentiation and specialization. Students may receive credit for one of the following: BICD 110 and BICD 110R.
courses.prerequisites_text: BIBC 100 or BIBC 102 or CHEM 114A or CHEM 114B.

courses.subject: BICD
courses.title: Plant Molecular Genetics and Biotechnology Laboratory
courses.description: Techniques in plant cell and tissue culture, plant transformation, genetic selection and screening of mutants, host pathogen interactions, gene regulation, organelle isolation, membrane transport. Attendance at the first lecture/lab is required. Nonattendance may result in the student being dropped from the course roster. Recommended preparation: BICD 120. Material lab fees will apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; BICD 100 or BICD 100R and BILD 4.

courses.subject: BICD
courses.title: Immunology
courses.description: Formation and function of the mammalian immune system, molecular and cellular basis of the immune response, infectious diseases and autoimmunity.
courses.prerequisites_text: BICD 100 or BICD 100R and BIMM 100. BIBC 100 recommended.

courses.subject: BICD
courses.title: Active Genetics
courses.description: An advanced introduction to non-Mendelian genetics with an emphasis on CRISPR-based mechanisms for achieving super-Mendelian inheritance of genetic traits. The course will provide a brief history of non-Mendelian genetics and then move on to the use of such systems for laboratory research or to alter populations of organisms either locally or more broadly to address issues of public health such as insecticide resistance and antibiotic resistance to support globally sustainable practices.
courses.prerequisites_text: BICD 100 or BICD 100R.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Human Physiology I
courses.description: Course introduces the concepts of physiological regulation, controlled and integrated by the nervous and endocrine systems. Course then examines the muscular, cardiovascular, and renal systems in detail and considers their control through the interaction of nervous activity and hormones. Note: Students may receive credit for one of the following: BIPN 100, BIPN 100R, or BENG 140A.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 1 and BILD 2.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Human Physiology II
courses.description: Course completes a survey of organ systems begun in BIPN 100 or BIPN 100R by considering the respiratory and gastrointestinal systems. Consideration is given to interactions of these systems in weight and temperature regulation, exercise physiology, stress, and pregnancy and reproduction. Note: Students may not receive credit for both BIPN 102 and BENG 140B.
courses.prerequisites_text: BIPN 100 or BIPN 100R.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Human Physiology Lab
courses.description: The focus of this course is to study human physiology. Experimental animals and human demonstrations are used to study membrane physiology, nerve and muscle function, hormone actions, cardiovascular physiology, and renal function. Students will also perform a research project and present their results in a symposium at the end of the quarter. Material lab fees will apply. Attendance at the first lecture/lab is required. Nonattendance may result in the student being dropped from the course roster.
courses.prerequisites_text: BIPN 100 or BIPN 100R.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Cellular Neurobiology
courses.description: This course covers the biophysics of the resting and active membranes of nerve cells. It also covers the mechanisms of sensory transduction and neuromodulation, as well as the molecular basis of nerve cell function.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 1 and BILD 2.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Developmental Neurobiology
courses.description: Molecular basis of neuronal cell fate determination, axon pathfinding, synaptogenesis experience-based refinement of connections, and learning in the brain will be examined.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Neurobiology Laboratory
courses.description: Students will gain experience with an array of methods used in modern neurobiology, including electrophysiology, optogenetics, and big data analysis. This laboratory course begins with the electric and chemical underpinnings of the nervous system and then dives into innovative techniques that we can use to study and change it. Attendance at the first lecture/lab is required. Nonattendance may result in the student being dropped from the course roster. Material lab fee will apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 2 and BILD 4 and MATH 11.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Computational Systems Neurobiology
courses.description: Models of neural coding and computation in the olfactory, visual, auditory, and somatosensory systems. Models of the motor system including central pattern generators, reinforcement learning, and motor cortex. Models of memory systems including working memory, long term memory, and memory consolidation. This course and BIPN 146 are taught in alternate years.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 2 and MATH 10A or MATH 20A and MATH 10B or MATH 20B and MATH 11.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: The Healthy and Diseased Brain
courses.description: Covers the clinical symptoms, treatment, and molecular mechanisms of neurological, neurodevelopmental, and neuropsychiatric disorders. Emphasis on understanding methods and developing the ability to read and evaluate the scientific literature.
courses.prerequisites_text: BIPN 140.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Neural Data Science
courses.description: Project-based course in which students will use computational notebooks to perform exploratory data analyses and to test hypotheses in large neuroscience data sets, including the differences between unique neuron types, leveraging text mining of the neuroscience literature, and human neuroimaging analyses.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 11 and BILD 62 or COGS 18 or CSE 8A. Students will use their own laptop computers.

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Computational Models and Theories in Neuroscience
courses.description: This course covers mathematical models of neurons, synapses, and neural networks. We will introduce theoretical frameworks of brain activity and function to understand neural computation and control of behavior. We will discuss network dynamics, synaptic plasticity, learning and memory. Students will apply modeling approaches to address scientific questions and make predictions for experiments.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or MATH 20A and MATH 10B or MATH 20B and MATH 11 and BILD 62 or BIPN 162 or COGS 18 or CSE 6R or CSE 8A. Students will use their own technology (e.g., laptops).

courses.subject: BIPN
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Modern Biology: Physiology and Neuroscience
courses.description: Course will vary in title and content. Students are expected to actively participate in course discussions, read, and analyze primary literature. Current descriptions and subtitles may be found on the Schedule of Classes and the School of Biological Sciences website . Students may receive credit in 194 courses a total of four times as topics vary. Students may not receive credit for the same topic.
courses.prerequisites_text: BIPN 140.

courses.subject: BIBC
courses.title: Metabolic Biochemistry
courses.description: Energy-producing pathways–glycolysis, the TCA cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, photosynthesis, and fatty acid oxidation; and biosynthetic pathways–gluconeogenesis, glycogen synthesis, and fatty acid biosynthesis. Nitrogen metabolism, urea cycle, amino acid metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, and metabolism of macromolecules.
courses.prerequisites_text: BENG 120 or CHEM 140A or CHEM 40A or CHEM 41A and BENG 120 or CHEM 140B or CHEM 40B or CHEM 41B. Note: Students may not receive credit for both BIBC 102 and CHEM 114B.

courses.subject: BIBC
courses.title: Biochemical Techniques
courses.description: Introductory laboratory course in current principles and techniques applicable to research problems in biochemistry and molecular biology. Techniques include protein and nucleic acid purification; identification methods such as centrifugation, chromatography, and electrophoresis; immunological, spectrophotometric, and enzymatic methods. Material lab fees will apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 1. Note: Students may not receive credit for BIBC 103 after taking CHEM 108. Attendance at the first lecture/lab is required. Nonattendance may result in the student’s being dropped from the course roster.

courses.subject: BIBC
courses.title: Gene Editing and Biotechnology
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of biotechnology including the principles of CRISPR-based gene editing technology. The course will cover various applications of biotechnology, with particular emphasis on crop domestication and improvement including commercialization of edited crops. Topics include genetic modifications by CRISPR, plant transformation, genetically modified foods, and policy/regulation of biotechnology.
courses.prerequisites_text: BICD 100 or BICD 100R.

courses.subject: BIBC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Modern Biology: Biochemistry
courses.description: Course will vary in title and content. Students are expected to actively participate in course discussions, read, and analyze primary literature. Current descriptions and subtitles may be found on the Schedule of Classes and the School of Biological Sciences website . Students may receive credit in 194 courses a total of four times as topics vary. Students may not receive credit for the same topic.
courses.prerequisites_text: BIBC 100 or BIBC 102 or CHEM 114A or CHEM 114B.

courses.subject: BGGN
courses.title: Communicating Science
courses.description: Learn effective ways of communicating science in both written and verbal form. Develop an understanding of how to effectively present science for different audiences, including writing for grants and papers, figure generation, and oral presentations. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. Enrollment restricted to the following major codes: BI77 and BI78.

courses.subject: BGGN
courses.title: Scientific Ethics
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SOMI 226.) Lectures, reading, and discussions about the responsible conduct and reporting of research, working with others in science, and social responsibilities; the course is designed as an option for meeting current federal regulations. S/U grades only. Enrollment restricted to PhD students only in the following major codes: BI77 and BI78. Students should review the following web page prior to enrollment: https://ethics.ucsd.edu/courses/ethics/index.html . Biology PhD students should enroll during spring of year two.

courses.subject: BGGN
courses.title: Applied Bioinformatics Lab
courses.description: Genomics and other “-omics” approaches are key tools for biology and medicine. This course provides a hands-on introduction to the computer-based analysis of genomic and biomolecular data.
